To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single reprogramming transcription factor Zfp521 alone can reprogram adult mouse astrocytes into NSCs in the absence of exogenous factors.
Zfp521‐induced NSCs can be generated from adult mouse astroglia and that these cells are capable of self‐renew and multipotency.
we show that a single reprogramming transcription factor, Zfp521, alone is sufficient for generating induced NSCs from adult astrocyte cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy for the production of iNSCs, which may be applied to the treatment of neurodegeneration.
the conversion of adult brain‐derived cells into iNSCs, which could be a new approach for cell therapy of neural injuries.
the generation of neural stem cells (iNSCs), which can be used in cell replacement therapy for treatment of brain diseases and injuries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Zfp521‐expressing iNSCs are a promising source for cell replacement therapy in the treatment of neurodegeneration and neural trauma.
ZFP521‐induced NSC generation from astrocytes is a promising approach for cell‐based therapy in the brain.
Zfp521 is a promising candidate factor for reprogramming of astrocytes into induced neural stem cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that a single reprogramming protein Zfp521 is sufficient for conversion of the adult mouse brain–derived astrocytes to neural stem cells in the absence of any extrinsic inductive factors.
Zfp521 is a promising factor for generating NSCs from astrocytes.
we identified Zfp521 as a single reprogramming protein that is capable of inducing astrocytes into NSCs in the absence of exogenous inductive signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Zfp521‐mediated astroglia reprogramming is a promising approach for the generation of iNSCs from the resident astrocytes in cell‐replacement therapies.
Zfp521 alone could convert astroglia into iNSCs and this conversion could be used in cell therapy for neural injuries.
Zfp521 is sufficient for converting astrocytes into NSCs.
